title: fix(ci): the cross-repo closer refuses a foreign PULL REQUEST, fails on a refusal, and gets a harness
body:
Fixes #5261

## This repository's own measurement, first

The card makes this the first deliverable because it decides whether the
pull-request defect is urgent or merely wrong. **It is not the framework's
number, and the difference is the headline.**

**Window: all 3,425 merged pull requests in this repository** — #1 through
#5288, merged 2026-01-13 through 2026-08-19. That is the complete merged
history, not a sample: the closed-PR listing was paged to exhaustion (3,605
closed PRs over 37 pages) and every body run through the workflow's own regex,
verbatim.

| | objectui (measured here) | framework (its own card's figure) |
|---|---|---|
| window | 3,425 merged PRs (all of them) | 1,176 most recently merged |
| merged PRs carrying a qualified **foreign** closing keyword | **60** (61 occurrences, 59 distinct targets) | **0** |
| of those targets, how many name a **pull request** | **0 of the 57 that resolve** | 0 |

Counter-probes, so the two zeros above are readings rather than a broken regex:
the same pattern finds **246** qualified *same-repo* references (which the loop
skips by design) and the bare-form spelling in **972** of the same merged PRs
(1,030 distinct targets).

Two of the 59 targets could not be classified from this session at all —
objectstack-ai/cloud#667 and objectstack-ai/cloud#654, named by #2045 and #2040:
this session's GitHub proxy answers 403 for that repository and `add_repo`
reports no access. Five more resolve only through repository renames
(`objectstack-ai/framework` is now `objectstack-ai/objectstack`,
`objectql/objectui` is now `objectstack-ai/objectui`); each of those five was
confirmed by matching the naming PR's own title to the target's title, and all
five are issues.

### The part that changes the severity, and it is not defect 1

This workflow landed here on 2026-08-09 (#3969) and has never been edited since.
In the ten days after that, **15** merged PRs carried a qualified foreign
closing keyword — roughly 1.5 a day. For every one of them:

- the framework issue was **closed by a seat one to two seconds after the
  merge**, which in 14 of the 15 is *before this workflow's run had even been
  created* (in the 15th the close lands in the same second the run is created,
  and the runner starts later still);
- so the loop read `state === 'closed'`, took the `already closed — skipping`
  branch, and skipped the target **whole**;
- **none of the 15 framework issues carries this workflow's backlink comment**,
  and **none of the 15 pull requests carries its token-absent notice**;
- all **941** runs of this workflow have reported success.

So the branch this file exists for has had a live target every day, taken
exactly one exit every time, delivered nothing on every one of them, and been
green throughout. Defect 3 in the card — the dropped backlink — is not a
theoretical half; it is the **only** behaviour this workflow has ever exhibited
here. Defect 1 is insurance, but insurance on a live path rather than a dead
one.

## What was ported, and from where

Ported from **objectstack-ai/objectstack `cb9ff23fab46ad504b8e6f617a56c207e7020edd`**
(the commit that last touched both files there), read off that repo's
`origin/main` at `a065e46550b48ee0b9189e947767ae188041208b`. The script block is
the framework's bytes; the only edits inside it are comments — repo-specific
cross-references qualified the way this repo spells them, three sentences that
would be false here rewritten (two named framework workflow files that do not
exist in this repository, and one quoted the framework's run counts). All four
hardening rounds come across together:

1. the notice path's declared retry policy, work order announced before
   delivery, and a refused notice that lands in the job summary and fails
   (objectstack-ai/objectstack#9575, #9594);
2. refusal accounting — the loop keeps its `catch` for isolation, records the
   keys it could not finish, and the verdict is passed after it
   (objectstack-ai/objectstack#9595);
3. backlink-on-closed, split three ways by `state_reason`, with a per-PR marker
   so a re-run is idempotent (objectstack-ai/objectstack#9643);
4. the `issue.pull_request` guard, placed **before** the already-closed branch
   (objectstack-ai/objectstack#9711).

Placement matters and is pinned: a merged pull request answers this endpoint
with `state: 'closed'` and `state_reason: null` — measured today on
objectstack-ai/objectstack#9143 and #9716 — which is exactly the fixture that
makes a closed *issue* get its backlink. A guard sitting after that branch would
still comment on somebody else's pull request. Scenario L13 is that ordering
test.

## The judgement the card left open: quiet, warn, or red

**Red — matching the framework's landed version**, which records both an
annotation (`core.warning` naming the target) and a post-loop `core.setFailed`
carrying the malformed class separately from the refusal class. Convergence is
the card's binding scope, and this is the choice that copy already made.

The measurement above supports it more strongly here than it did there, and the
affordability was re-derived against this repository rather than inherited:

- the `main` ruleset (11776024) carries `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`,
  `merge_queue` and `pull_request` rules and **no `required_status_checks` rule
  at all**, so no context is required on this repository today;
- the job runs only after the merge, so its conclusion gates nothing that has
  not already happened;
- **no `workflow_run:` listener exists in this repository**, so a red starts no
  fan-out.

A red therefore costs one X on an already-merged PR. Against that: 941 green
runs, 15 of which delivered nothing, and nobody noticed until this card. A green
run of this job has never been opened by anybody here — which is precisely why
an annotation on a green post-merge run is the quiet path with extra steps.

## The harness, and the file surface it needed

`scripts/check-cross-repo-closer-outcome.mjs` is the framework harness, adapted
to this side of the pair (this repo is `thisRepo`, so the foreign fixture is a
framework target and the skipped same-repo one is ours). It extracts the shipped
script out of the YAML with a real parser and runs it as one AsyncFunction body,
the way `actions/github-script` does — never a retyped copy — and every failure
to extract is a failure rather than a skip.

**Declared surface, wider than the card's:** the card scoped this to the
workflow plus the script and harness under `scripts/`. Two additions were
needed and are both here:

- `.github/workflows/lint.yml` — the wiring. Without it the harness runs
  nowhere, and the self-test asserts the wiring is present, so this is not
  optional (it was red on exactly those two assertions until the step landed).
- `package.json` plus `pnpm-lock.yaml` — `extractScript` needs a real YAML
  parser. `yaml@2.9.0` was already resolved in this lockfile as a transitive, so
  the delta is three lines and no new package version enters the tree. The
  framework declares the same `yaml: ^2.9.0` at its root.

No changeset: `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` reports 4 files
changed, 0 under the `src/` of a released package, and exits 0.

## Verification — executed, not reasoned about

All at `a5a0678ac`, the commit this PR is opened on.

Executed:

```
$ node scripts/check-cross-repo-closer-outcome.mjs --self-test
✓ check-cross-repo-closer-outcome --self-test: 77 assertions, 14 mutations of the shipped script each driven to red.

$ node scripts/check-cross-repo-closer-outcome.mjs
check-cross-repo-closer-outcome: OK (105 assertions over 18 scenarios, driving the 18420-char script extracted from .github/workflows/cross-repo-issue-closer.yml).
```

**Reverse verification — the battery driven at the PRE-PORT script.** The module
is inert on import by design, so `judge` can be pointed at another tree. The
same 105 checks against this repo's `origin/main` copy of the workflow produce
**40 failed assertions**, including exactly the two the card asks to see proven:

```
=== PRE-PORT  (origin/main copy) — 40 failed assertion(s) over 105 checks ===
  [L3] L3 FAILS the job -- the defect this card is about; got 0
  [L3] L3 setFailed names the target left open
  [L12] L12 does NOT close the pull request -- GitHub's own keyword parser never closes one ...
  [L12] L12 still closes the other two targets -- isolation holds; got 3
  ...
=== PORTED    (this branch) — 0 failed assertion(s) over 105 checks ===
```

L3 is the simulated refusal: one target's `issues.get` is refused with HTTP 404
while the other two stay reachable. The pre-port script calls `core.setFailed`
**zero** times on it — green on a refusal — and the ported one goes red while
still closing the other two. L12's `got 3` is the pull-request defect in the
same run: the pre-port script closed all three targets, one of which is a PR.

Also executed, green: `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs`,
`node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`,
`node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`,
`node scripts/check-lint-coverage.mjs`,
`node scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`,
`node scripts/check-node-esm-load.mjs`,
`node scripts/check-phantom-dependencies.mjs`,
`node scripts/check-action-forward-parity.mjs`,
`node scripts/check-published-dist-tooling.mjs`,
`node scripts/check-skills-paths.mjs`,
`npx eslint scripts/check-cross-repo-closer-outcome.mjs`, and
`vitest run --project unit scripts/__tests__` — **55 files, 1,272 tests, all
passing**, which includes the four that pin these workflows
(`ci-cd-pipeline-doc`, `lint-workflow`, `merge-queue-reporting`,
`dependabot-merge-gate`).

**YAML validity and the credential walk**, machine-diffed old against new rather
than eyeballed. Unchanged: the trigger (`pull_request_target`, `types: [closed]`),
the top-level permissions (`contents: read`, `pull-requests: write`), the absence
of job-level permissions, the `merged == true` gate, the action version, the
`github-token` expression, and the step `env`. Added: the two step inputs
`retries: 3` and `retry-exempt-status-codes: 400,401,404,422`, which change how
often a request is asked and no verdict anywhere. The script's API surface gains
exactly one method, `issues.listComments` — read-only, on a repository the token
already comments on and closes in.

**Not executed** (and not claimable): GitHub Actions cannot run locally, so no
statement here is made about a real run of the workflow. Everything above about
its behaviour comes from the harness driving the shipped bytes under doubles, or
from the API measurements described at the top.
